To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can: (1) Learn from web and social media images with associated text a multimodal image text embedding that can be used for semantic image retrieval, (2) Learn from web images with associated text embeddings that can be used to retrieve visually similar images, (3) Transfer the learned knowledge from text embeddings to visual models to improve the performance of image retrieval tasks.

(a) we can learn a multimodal representation of images and text from web data, (b) we can leverage the semantic knowledge in this representation to perform semantic image retrieval, and (c) we propose a new dataset for fair comparison of multimodal image and video embeddings.

(1) we propose a new method for learning multimodal image and word embeddings from web data without supervision and demonstrate that they can be used to perform semantic image retrieval tasks, (2) we propose a novel dataset of 1M Instagram images and their text descriptions for fair comparison of text image embedding methods, and (3) we show that the proposed pipeline outperforms the state of the-art on the MIRFlicker dataset, and that the learned embeddings are competitive to supervised methods
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can a text embedding trained with web data be used to improve the performance of an image retrieval system?
the following questions: (1) Can we leverage web and social media images and texts to learn a joint image and text representation? (2) Can the learned embedding be used for semantic image retrieval?

the following main contributions: (1) We show that self supervised learning from web data can be used to learn a joint multimodal image and textual embedding space, (2) we show that this embedding is competitive with supervised methods for the text based image search task and outperforms the state of the-art in the MIRflickr dataset (3) we show that our embedding can be used for semantic image retrieval and (4) we release a new dataset, composed of 1M Instagram images
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the learned text embeddings from web data are competitive with the supervised ones in the text based retrieval tasks, while they are not competitive with the supervised models in the visual retrieval tasks.
the proposed method learns a multimodal image-text embedding from web data that can be used for semantic image retrieval, and is able to outperform supervised baselines.
the best text embedding is the one learned from the target domain, but the best text embeddings learned from web data are competitive to supervised methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new approach to learn multimodal image and textual embeddings from web and social media, we present a novel dataset for this purpose and we demonstrate that the learned embeddings are able to outperform the state-of-the art in the text based retrieval problem.
the learned embeddings can be used to perform multimodal semantic retrieval with no human annotation, and can be used as an initial point for fine tuning with a target dataset.

we show how to learn multimodal embeddings from web and social media platforms without human supervision, and we demonstrate that the learned representations can be used to perform semantic image retrieval, going beyond classical image retrieval problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self supervised learning from free available web and social media multimodal data is a powerful and scalable alternative to traditional supervised learning.
self supervised learning from free available data can be used to learn competitive image text representations, and it can be used to solve challenging semantic image retrieval problems.
self supervised learning from web data allows to leverage the knowledge of the semantic space of the texts to learn visual representations for image retrieval.
